alternate_names: Sri Mallikarjuna Swamy Kamakshi Tayee Ammavari Temple
deities: Kamakshi (Shakti, combined form of Kali and Matangi)

history.dynasty: Chola-era; 1150 AD (per inscriptions and district records); local chief Manumasiddhi's patronage; Sri Chakra installed by Adi Shankaracharya (traditional, 4th century per legend)
history.period: 12th century (present temple 1150 AD); legendary origins in the Treta Yuga
history.summary: The principal Devi temple of southern Andhra on the banks of the Penna at Jonnawada village (Buchireddipalem mandal), about 12-15 km from Nellore. Skanda Purana legend says sage Kasyapa performed a yagna with three kundas at Rajathagiri and Shiva emerged from the fire as the Mallikarjuna linga; the goddess's idol, found by fishermen in a net in the Penna, was installed beside him by Adi Shankaracharya along with a Sri Chakra, pacifying her into benign form. The present temple dates to 1150 AD; its entrance door, dwajasthambham and gopuram carry five gold-plated kalashams. Kasyapa Theertham lake near the temple is believed to wash away sins. name: Sri Mallikarjuna Swamy Kamakshi Temple, Jonnawada
town_description: Jonnawada is a village in Buchireddipalem mandal of Nellore district, on the banks of the Penna river about 12-15 km from Nellore city. It is a well-known pilgrimage centre for the 12th-century Mallikarjuna Swamy-Kamakshi temple, with devasthanam and TTD choultries for visiting pilgrims.

travel.airport: Tirupati International Airport, about 143 km away.
travel.railway: Nellore railway station, about 15 km away.
travel.road: About 12 km by bus from Nellore; regular bus services from Nellore to Jonnawada.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Vaisakha Brahmotsavams draw lakhs of devotees; Fridays are special for Kamakshi worship.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Official district listing: 5:00 AM-1:00 PM and 4:30 PM-9:15 PM (verify: one source lists 6:00 AM-12:00 PM and 2:00 PM-8:00 PM).
